body:
`#766` added `ARG GIT_SHA` / `ENV GIT_SHA` to `apps/mcp-hub/Dockerfile` and surfaced it at `GET /health`, but this workflow's `docker build` passed **no** `--build-arg` — so the ARG default stood and every image reported `git_sha: "unknown"`. The observable shipped inert. The release gate on #766 found it; that PR's body has been corrected to stop claiming otherwise.

This is the half OPS-108 could not do: `.github/workflows/**` is forbidden by that bead's scope, which is why this is a separate change and why bead [`83cafa82`](83cafa82-e1d5-451d-9731-e4f6cc51e3a3) (OPS-109) exists to carry it.

Outer-loop: true

Change kind: behavioral

## Ordering — load-bearing

This lands **after** #766 (merged as `49c8728`). `build-mcp-hub.yml` triggers on pushes to `main` touching its own path, so merging this first would have built a `main` that still carried the `IndexError`, and #756's smoke test would correctly have failed it — a red build that reads as though this change broke something.

## Why the Dockerfile placement matters

The `ARG`/`ENV` pair sits **below** every expensive layer in the Dockerfile (moved there at the gate, #766 commit `beaf467`). An `ENV` whose value changes invalidates the cache for everything after it — so with the pair at the top, passing a per-commit value here would make every merge re-run `apt-get`, the `uv` install and a full dependency resolve against this job's 600s timeout on the self-hosted runner. Do not move it back up.

## Verification Evidence

- Workflow still parses as YAML, and the step renders the intended command:
  ```
  timeout 600s docker build \
    --build-arg GIT_SHA="${GITHUB_SHA}" \
    -t mcp-hub:latest apps/mcp-hub/
  ```
- Confirmed before the change that `docker build` at `build-mcp-hub.yml:34` was the only `docker build` in the workflow and carried no `--build-arg`.
- The real test is the next build: `/health`'s `git_sha` must equal this merge commit rather than `unknown`. Until this lands, `git_sha` proves nothing and must not be cited as evidence of what is deployed.
